question: How much does a fixed 12-rune opening constrain an otherwise arbitrary 29-entry feedback substitution table?
input: LP2-00..55 excluding runeless LP2-50; first 24 recognized runes including headings on each page; nine existing fixed 12-rune known-reading openings.
field: Canonical Gematria Primus indices 0..28, all arithmetic modulo 29.
modes: CTA: for i=1..11, P_i=C_i−f(C_(i−1)); equivalently f(C_(i−1))=C_i−P_i.
PTA: for i=1..11, P_i=C_i−f(P_(i−1)); equivalently f(P_(i−1))=C_i−P_i.
first_symbol: P_0 is stipulated by the crib; an external primer or rule must account for it. It creates no f-table constraint.
compatibility: The same input index must imply the same f output every time. If so, r distinct inputs are assigned and exactly 29^(29−r) full functions F29→F29 extend the partial table; otherwise zero do.
held_forward: For a consistent opening, inspect positions 12..23 on that same page only. CTA reports individually determined positions where C_(i−1) already has an assigned table value. PTA advances from the stipulated P_11 until f(current plaintext) is first undefined; it reports only this initial chain. No future plaintext is available as a truth label, so no validation claim is made.
size: Two modes × 55 page starts × nine openings = 990 finite crib/table-inference cases; not an enumeration of the 29^29 full functions.
controls: Independent constraint construction from page JSON, planted known-table checks for both modes, inconsistent repeated-input controls, and exhaustive all-function comparison over F3 and F5 for synthetic cases.
exclusions: Search over primer rules, unknown plaintext, scored English, further ciphertext layers, page shifts, alternative alphabet order, variable feedback state and claims of a verified LP2 decryption.
